response.message:
I've drawn a full Google Cloud sketch for a support agent's assistant on a synthetic call. Consent comes first, and audio stops there if the caller declines. Approved audio then goes through Speech-to-Text, and Sensitive Data Protection removes personal details before Gemini sees anything. Gemini suggests answers grounded in Vertex AI Search, drafts a summary for the agent to approve, and prepares a CRM update the agent applies by hand. Nothing places calls or writes to the CRM automatically.

For the first local test, we'd play a synthetic audio clip with a scripted transcript and planted fake personal details. That checks the consent gate, that redaction runs before the model, the approval steps, and that no CRM write ever happens. The model replies in that test are scripted. They prove the wiring works, not answer quality. To validate the model for real, we'd run Gemini on Vertex AI in an approved project and region against a labelled set of synthetic calls. That needs access we haven't checked, and nothing is deployed, so the region is still "to be selected."

Which CRM is the existing one, and should the assistant read customer context from it during the call, or only produce the draft update?

response.message:
The emulation check didn't find a fault in our design: it reports no test failures, and the whole flow is still connected from consent through redaction to agent approval, with no automatic CRM write. It's blocked only because the export tool has no generator yet for these eight Google Cloud components (Cloud Run consent and streaming services, Speech-to-Text, Sensitive Data Protection, Vertex AI Search, the orchestrator, Gemini) or a plan to reference the existing call source. Changing the diagram can't fix that, and swapping in a supported storage-only contract would cut the scope you asked for, so I've left the board as it is. Building those generators is product engineering work, and this report plus artifact e119feab… is the reproducer.

Meanwhile, let's settle a decision that will matter whichever services we end up building: should the assistant read customer context from the existing CRM during the call (and if so, which CRM is it), or should it only prepare the draft update for the agent to apply by hand?
